newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger bans opposition poll anniversary protest.
newsitem.headline: Niger bans opposition poll anniversary protest.

text.p: Niger's government has banned opposition protests to mark the first anniversary of chaotic elections in which President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara made the transition from coup leader to elected head of state.

Interior Minister Idi Ango Omar told state television late on Wednesday that the government had banned all demonstrations on July 7 and 8 after receiving reports that violent protests were being planned.

"We cannot, in conformity with the penal code, tolerate demonstrations aimed at continually disturbing public order and inciting citizens to rise up and take arms against the authority of the state and against one another," he said.
Mainassara, who toppled elected president Mahamane Ousmane in January 1996, scrapped the independent electoral commission on day-two of polling last July.
Security forces took control of ballot boxes and the count took place in the absence of representatives of opposition political parties.
The opposition cried foul and refused to accept the result. The United States suspended aid in protest.

Ango Omar said that the supreme court had confirmed the election results. He denounced opposition parties for continuing to reject the result, saying that bowing to the law of the land was a condition of life in society.
He said regional and sub-regional authorities would take the necessary steps to maintain public order on the anniversary.
Mainassara took power after a standoff between Mahamane and his prime minister paralysed government for over a year.
